cases.name: sequential-text-loops
cases.description: Values come out in order and start again at the end
cases.config: <tdc><env count="7" seed="demo" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="M"><gen type="text" value="Jan,Feb,Mar" order="sequential"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{M}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: sequential-exact-length
cases.description: cycle="false" is fine when the count matches the list exactly
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="demo" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="M"><gen type="text" value="Jan,Feb,Mar" order="sequential" cycle="false"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{M}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: sequential-takes-no-draws
cases.description: Walking a list in order consumes no randomness
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="demo" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="M"><gen type="text" value="Jan,Feb,Mar" order="sequential"/></sequence><sequence name="N"><gen type="number" value="100..999"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{M}} ${{N}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-fixed-repeat-walks-the-list-inside-one-row
cases.description: The order lifecycle in one sequence: four steps, in order, on every row. Element k of row r takes source index r*N+k, and with a list of four and repeat="4" that is the whole list each time — which is the config this combination was invented for.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="V"><gen type="text" value="created,paid,shipped,delivered" order="sequential" repeat="4"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{V}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: the-walk-carries-on-across-rows
cases.description: The part a single row cannot show: three values taken two at a time do not restart at every row, they continue. Row 0 takes a,b — row 1 takes c,a. An implementation that restarted the walk per row would print a,b six times and pass any test that only looked at one row.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="V"><gen type="text" value="a,b,c" order="sequential" repeat="2"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{V}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: repeat-one-is-the-plain-walk
cases.description: The property that makes carrying on the right rule rather than a second meaning: at repeat="1" the column is exactly what order="sequential" alone has always produced. The case above it in this file walks the same list without a repeat and must print the same values.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="V"><gen type="text" value="a,b,c" order="sequential" repeat="1"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{V}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: the-same-walk-without-a-repeat
cases.description: The twin of the case above, written out rather than described, because a claim about two configs is only checked when both are run.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="V"><gen type="text" value="a,b,c" order="sequential"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{V}}</data></line></block></tdc>
